about.title: Whittier Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails should not become your problem to prove. In Whittier, that might be a space heater that ignites in an apartment off Beverly Boulevard, a ladder that buckles during a weekend project, or a child's car seat that comes apart in a fender-bender on Painter Avenue. California treats most of these claims under strict liability. Instead of showing that a company was careless, you generally need to show the product had a defect — in its design, in how it was made, or in the warnings that came with it — and that the defect caused your injury. The reach of that rule is wide: the manufacturer, the distributor, and the store on Whittier Boulevard that sold it may each share responsibility. Whittier's 87,438 residents buy the same tools, appliances, medications, and vehicles as the rest of Los Angeles County, and when one of them fails, LawProactive connects you at no cost with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency. Keep the product. Do not repair, return, or discard it.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was negligent?
items.answer: Usually not. California product liability commonly runs on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective in its design, manufacturing, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company meant well or acted carelessly is often beside the point. An attorney can tell you which theory fits your situation.

items.question: A part on my car failed in a crash on Lambert Road. Is that a product case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It may be both. Whittier recorded 443 injury collisions in 2025, and some crashes involve a defective airbag, brake, or tire alongside a driver's mistake. A product liability claim can be brought against the manufacturer or seller even while a separate claim runs against another driver. Keep the vehicle and the failed part exactly as they are until an attorney has weighed in.

items.question: I threw away the packaging. Can I still bring a claim in Whittier?
items.answer: Possibly. The product itself matters most, so hold onto it in its current condition and photograph everything you still have. Receipts, bank statements, and photos of where you bought it can help trace the retailer and distributor. LawProactive will connect you at no cost with an independent attorney who can assess what remains.
